import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Router component that directs claims to three output ports based on ordered rules.
    Rules are evaluated in order; a row matches the FIRST applicable rule only.
    Unmatched rows go to the default port 'standard' (which is not in the outputs).
    """
    claims = inputs['claims'].copy()
    
    # Initialize output dataframes
    fast_track = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    high_value = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    manual_review = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    
    # Track which rows have been matched
    matched = pd.Series([False] * len(claims), index=claims.index)
    
    # Rule 1: amount <= 500 and photos_attached == 1 → fast_track
    rule1_mask = (claims['amount'] <= 500) & (claims['photos_attached'] == 1)
    rule1_rows = rule1_mask & ~matched
    fast_track = pd.concat([fast_track, claims[rule1_rows]], ignore_index=False)
    matched = matched | rule1_rows
    
    # Rule 2: amount > 10000 → high_value
    rule2_mask = claims['amount'] > 10000
    rule2_rows = rule2_mask & ~matched
    high_value = pd.concat([high_value, claims[rule2_rows]], ignore_index=False)
    matched = matched | rule2_rows
    
    # Rule 3: photos_attached == 0 or amount > 500 → manual_review
    rule3_mask = (claims['photos_attached'] == 0) | (claims['amount'] > 500)
    rule3_rows = rule3_mask & ~matched
    manual_review = pd.concat([manual_review, claims[rule3_rows]], ignore_index=False)
    matched = matched | rule3_rows
    
    # Reset index to ensure clean integer indices
    fast_track = fast_track.reset_index(drop=True)
    high_value = high_value.reset_index(drop=True)
    manual_review = manual_review.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Select only the required columns for output
    output_columns = ['claim_id', 'amount', 'photos_attached']
    
    return {
        'claims_fast_track': fast_track[output_columns] if len(fast_track) > 0 else pd.DataFrame(columns=output_columns),
        'claims_high_value': high_value[output_columns] if len(high_value) > 0 else pd.DataFrame(columns=output_columns),
        'claims_manual_review': manual_review[output_columns] if len(manual_review) > 0 else pd.DataFrame(columns=output_columns)
    }
